title: Practice Test 2 · sequencing and scheduling
source: Exercises to practice, Second Test (F. Martinez, 10 Nov 2025) and its answer key
intro: Draw it! Cycles = order / (P · S), rounded up. Gradual: add every operation. Parallel: start from the longest operation, add the head (first cycles before it) and the tail (last units after it). DBR: drum + tail. Ask whether the setup needs the units of the previous operation.

exercises.text: You must manufacture 20 units of a new product.

parts.q: a) Gradual lead time, setup needs the units (min)

parts.model: Operation 2's setup runs while operation 1 works: 60 + 75 + 80 + 70 = 285.

parts.q: b) Parallel, setup needs the units (min)
parts.model: Longest: operation 2 (20 + 5 · 15 = 95). Head: op 1 10 + 10 = 20. Tail: op 2's last 4 units → op 3 2 cycles = 16 → op 3's last 2 units → op 4 1 cycle = 7. 20 + 95 + 16 + 7 = 138.
Longest without setups: op 3 (80). Head: op 1 20, op 2 one cycle 15 → op 3 starts at 35; 35 + 80 + op 4 tail 7 = 122.

parts.q: c) 21 units: gradual, setup needs units (min)
c) 21 units: parallel, setup needs units (min)

parts.model: Drum: op 3 = 80, then op 4's last cycle 7 = 87.

exercises.text: A manufacturing order of 23 units. Note: the task gives 12 min for operation D, but the answer key's table uses 11 min (giving 200 / 167, 107 / 101, 98 / 46). Here the task's 12 min is used.

parts.q: a) Gradual, setup needs the units (min)

parts.model: A 21 → B starts at 35 (its setup) → 75 → C 115 → D 163 → E 171 (key with D = 11: 167).

parts.q: b) Parallel, setup needs the units (min)
parts.model: Longest: B = 35 + 40 = 75. Head: A 5 + 2 · 2 = 9 (B takes 6 units). Tail: B's last 5 units → C 2 cycles = 10 → C's last 2 → D 1 cycle = 12 → E 2. 9 + 75 + 10 + 12 + 2 = 108 (key: 107).
Longest without setups: D = 4 · 12 = 48. B's 35-min setup is longer than A's 9, so B starts at 35; C feeds D after 2 cycles (55); 55 + 48 + E 2 = 105 (key: 101).

parts.q: c) One more unit (24). What changes?
parts.model: 23 and 24 units need the same number of cycles in every operation, so nothing changes.

parts.q: d) DBR, setup needs the units (min)

exercises.text: Steve Smith, a web designer, returns from vacation to five jobs, coded I to V in order of arrival. He wants to minimise the average time the jobs are in his office and, if possible, meet the due dates.

parts.model: III II I IV V: lateness 0, 5, 9, 9, 14 → 37 / 5.
SOT has the lowest average time (7.6) and the lowest average lateness (3). In the Gantt chart the jobs run V, IV, I, II, III over 17 working days (weekends skipped).
